subject: Hosted API — Volume Discount & Rate Protections
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@stratahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API pricing structure and rate protections

Rafael —

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As we evaluate Redwood for our primary inference tier, Procurement has two principal concerns we need to address before we can move to a pilot: clear volume discount bands for per-token usage and contractual protections against sharp price increases.

High level asks from my side:
- A simple, per-month tiered discount schedule (tokens/month -> discount %) and how overage is handled.
- A proposal for a price lock period tied to a committed monthly spend (we'd prefer 12 months).
- MFN or equivalent guarantee so we’re not paying more than comparable customers under the same terms.
- A cap on indexation — we live in a regulated budget environment and cannot accept open-ended CPI-linked increases; procurement suggested a CPI cap or fixed percent cap (they mentioned ~3% as a starting point).

I attached our RFP questions to make sure we cover procurement’s language. Can you share a draft commercial term sheet and confirm if Redwood can do a 12-month price lock + an MFN carve-out?

Appreciate it — we’re hoping to get to legal review this month.

— Alex
StrataHealth
attachment: StrataHealth_RFP_Qs.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@stratahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing structure and rate protections

Alex —

Thanks for the clear summary and the RFP — super helpful. I pulled together an initial commercial sketch for your team. Attached: Redwood_Strata_Draft_Proposal_v1.pdf which includes a tiered per-token discount schedule and a couple of optional terms for rate stability. Highlights here:

- Tiered discounts (monthly usage):
  - 0–250M tokens: list price
  - 250M–1B tokens: 10% off list
  - 1B–3B tokens: 18% off list
  - 3B+ tokens: custom tier (negotiated)
- Overage handling: monthly true-up at applied tier; we can include a smoothing clause for burst months if preferred.
- Price lock: we can offer a 12-month price lock tied to a minimum committed spend (commonly a monthly ARR commitment).
- MFN: Redwood is open to MFN-lite: parity on published list price and on-hosted discounts for the same customer tier. Full MFN across all customers is tougher operationally, but we can discuss scoped MFN to comparable enterprise customers.
- CPI cap: we typically index at published list with a floor, but we can propose a cap — 3% cap is reasonable for a 12-month term with a multi-year commitment.

Next steps:
1) Quick call to align commercial expectations (15–20 min).
2) If aligned, we'll put a redlineable term summary for procurement and legal.

Are you available tomorrow 10–11am PT?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
(415) 555-0148
attachment: Redwood_Strata_Draft_Proposal_v1.pdf

From: Alex Rivera <alex@stratahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-16T08:09:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing structure and rate protections

Rafael —

Thanks for the sketch and the quick cadence. Call tomorrow works. A couple of clarifications procurement flagged after reviewing your draft:

1) MFN scope: procurement wants assurance that, for the duration of our agreement, if Redwood offers materially better POR (price/other terms) to another customer in our segment (SMB vs enterprise differences ok), StrataHealth would receive parity. Is there precedent for a parity commitment scoped to our seat/usage tier?

2) CPI vs fixed cap: Procurement is okay with indexing off CPI-U but wants a hard cap (they suggested 3.0% as the max annual increase). Alternatively, they proposed a ‘‘price holdback’’ where a portion of credits are escrowed and released if price increases exceed X% in a year — curious if Redwood has implemented any escrow-style mitigations.

3) Term/renewal: if we lock price for 12 months, what’s the uplift mechanism on renewal — auto CPI with cap, or a negotiated outcome?

Procurement will join the call tomorrow and would like examples of language you can provide in a term summary.

Regards,
Alex

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API pricing structure and rate protections (StrataHealth)

Team — forwarding Strata’s procurement questions. Key asks: MFN scoped to comparable customers, 12-month price lock, CPI indexing with a hard annual cap (~3%), and an escrow-style holdback suggestion.

Monica: can you confirm technical alignment on burst smoothing and whether we should include a smoothing clause for token spikes? Also, can you help craft the operational definition of "comparable customer" for an MFN-lite?

Laura: if we want to move on a scoped MFN + 12-month lock at the discount tiers in my draft, what concession do we need to protect margin? My thinking: require a minimum monthly committed spend at the 1B tier to get the 18% discount with a 12-month price lock and a 3% annual cap. Alternatively, if they insist on a holdback/escrow mechanism, we should tie release events to usage goals or renewal.

I attached an updated pricing model that includes example math for a 12-month lock + CPI cap — see pricing_model_v2.xlsx. Looking for quick guidance so I can prepare a redline term summary for Alex and procurement before tomorrow's call.

— Rafael
attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@stratahealth.com>, procurement@stratahealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API — Draft term summary and next steps

Alex / Procurement team —

Appreciate the call earlier this week. Per our conversation, attached is a short, redlineable term summary that captures the agreed commercial guardrails:

- Discount schedule: as previously provided (0–250M: list; 250M–1B: 10%; 1B–3B: 18%; 3B+: custom).
- 12-month price lock: effective from contract signature provided StrataHealth meets a minimum monthly committed spend (specified in attached term summary).
- MFN-lite: Redwood will provide parity on publicly published hosted discount levels and on negotiated discount bands for customers in the same enterprise usage tier. MFN excludes special one-off concessions tied to product bundles or experimental programs.
- CPI indexation: list price may be adjusted annually but capped at 3.0% per 12-month period.
- Escrow/holdback option: we proposed an optional holdback of up to 5% of quarterly invoice value to be held in escrow and released after annual reconciliation if year-over-year price movement stays within agreed bounds; this is optional and requires an approved operational flow.

Attachments: Redwood_Strata_Term_Summary_v1.pdf (redline-ready). Also included is a DocuSign preview link for convenience. If this aligns, I’ll route a formal SOW and a DocuSign packet for signature by end of week.

Next steps:
1) Confirm MFN-lite language and whether procurement wants escrow included in the initial contract or as an amendment.
2) We’ll draft final SOW and DocuSign packet (3 business days).

Looking forward — happy to jump back on a short call to walk legal through the language.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
